title: AI governance is becoming operational infrastructure, not only policy language

signal.summary: AI governance is moving from principles and guidelines toward runtime controls, approvals, audit trails, and execution boundaries.
signal.why_now: Organizations are adopting agentic systems faster than their existing review and accountability processes can control them.

context: The practical gap is no longer only model capability. The gap is controlled execution: who can act, under which policy, with which evidence, and with what audit trail.
systemic_effects: Governance becomes a runtime requirement rather than a document-only requirement.
Approval centers, source tracking, and audit evidence become product features.
Trustworthy AI systems need visible limits, not only better prompts.
next_orientation_step: Map which AI actions are draft-only, which require human approval, and which are blocked until signed connectors exist.
